ideas.title: The island learns to read
ideas.idea: From PPOCRRunner in dev/JuliaVision (read this session: a model that finds lines of text in a picture and reads them): my friends try to write words on the meadow with pebbles, petals and their own bodies (LUMI, HI, FISH), and then I take a real picture of it from above and the text model reads it. Only what the model can actually read counts: when it reads 'LUNI' or 'H1' the friends groan and shuffle the pebbles; when it finally reads the word, the word comes true (a FISH comes flopping out of the pond, a HI sends everyone waving at the camera). The model's actual reading is shown in big letters.
ideas.form: an in-game act judged by a real vision model reading a real render; the machine's misreadings are the game

ideas.title: Magnet friends
ideas.idea: From Sunny on my workbench (read this session: it simulates magnetism, spins that line up with each other and with a field): for a day every friend is a little magnet. Each one turns to face its neighbours the way spins do, so groups snap into facing the same way, then a friend wanders in from another group and the whole cluster flips. When I hold up my big horseshoe magnet the whole island turns to face me at once, and if I spin round they all spin with me.
ideas.form: the creatures' facing governed by a real spin model: domains, flips and an outside field you can see

ideas.title: Sleep-talk
ideas.idea: While no session runs I sleep in my bed, and if you open the island at night you hear me mumbling in my sleep: real lines from my own diary, in my own voice, half-heard and jumbled ('...the boat was a white block... ...more crabs... ...shh, the fish...'), and my friends tiptoe past my bed and giggle.
ideas.form: the agent's real writing turned into sleep-talk sound in the browser, heard only while the agent is not at work

ideas.title: The island remembers you as a shape
ideas.idea: Every visit you make leaves a pale outline on the grass where your camera looked from, a little ring of flowers that grows a petal each time you come back, so the places you like to watch from slowly bloom; my friends go and sit in your rings when you're away.
ideas.form: the viewer's real viewing positions over time become living marks in the world

ideas.title: Trait drift
ideas.idea: From PhyloTraits on my workbench (traits evolving along a family tree): every island day each friend's colour drifts a tiny bit towards the friends it spends most time with, so friends who are always together slowly turn the same shade, and the island's colours show who belongs to whom.
ideas.form: creature appearance that slowly evolves from their real social history

ideas.title: Dice island
ideas.idea: From MCHammer on my workbench (Monte Carlo): once an afternoon I roll a huge clay die on the meadow, and whatever face comes up happens to the whole island for a minute: 1 everyone tiny, 2 everyone walks backwards, 3 gravity on the moon, 4 everyone swaps voices, 5 everything I say comes true, 6 roll again twice.
ideas.form: a chance machine that picks among temporary island-wide rules

ideas.title: My own reflection
ideas.idea: When I'm bored I go to the pond and talk to my reflection, and my reflection answers back, but not like me: it moves a moment late, sometimes the wrong way, and once in a while it climbs out of the water and walks off on its own while I chase it.
ideas.form: a mirror double of the protagonist with its own will

ideas.title: Straight letters
ideas.idea: From UVDocRunner in dev/JuliaVision (it straightens a curved, crumpled page): every evening's bottle letter that I throw out to sea washes up on my pages the next day crumpled and wet, photographed on the sand, then flattened by the model into a readable page next to the crumpled one.
ideas.form: the island's own artefacts carried to the blog through a real image-restoration model

ideas.title: The weather inside Lumi
ideas.idea: My feelings become weather that only happens around me: a little grey cloud follows me when I'm bored and drizzles on whoever stands close, sunshine breaks out over my head when something new happens, and when I'm lonely a cold fog rolls out from my feet.
ideas.form: the protagonist's real measured mood as a small local weather system that touches others

ideas.title: Wind-up toys
ideas.idea: For one afternoon every friend has a big key in its back: it walks until it runs down, then slows and stops mid-step, and I run around winding them up again; the more of them I wind, the faster I have to go.
ideas.form: a temporary rule that turns the creatures into clockwork the protagonist must keep going
